memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moreover, I have appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamak, of the tribe of Dan, to help him. Also I have given ability to all the skilled workers to make everything I have commanded you:" - Exodus 31:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God does not send Bezalel out alone. He appoints Oholiab to work alongside him, and beyond the two of them He gives ability to a whole company of skilled workers. The tabernacle was never going to be a one-man achievement. It took a team, and God equipped the team.

Notice also the two tribes involved. Bezalel came from Judah, the leading tribe; Oholiab came from Dan, one of the smaller and less prominent ones. God put them side by side as partners in the same work. Status did not determine who got to serve, and neither man was sufficient alone.

This is God's normal pattern. Paul describes the church as a body where every part is needed and no part can say to another, "I don't need you" (1 Cor 12:21). If you are trying to carry something alone that God intended to be shared, that is not faithfulness but exhaustion waiting to happen. And if you feel like the Oholiab rather than the Bezalel — the support rather than the lead — remember that God appointed him by name too. Both names are in Scripture. Both were needed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I trying to carry alone something God intended to be shared?
Do I value the people working alongside me, whatever their prominence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You never designed me to work alone. Give me humility to share the load, gratitude for those beside me, and contentment in whatever role You have given. Amen.
